items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: He was a pretty good teacher. He taught a lot of people around Chicago, including myself... Roy Palmer got me my first job... they really helped me immensely.

ctx.x: You don't remember that? No, I was small. When you were a baby there?

Yeah, I was a baby, you know. And I moved from up there, and in fact my parents did. They moved from there on to Palmer's Avenue. And so I must have been about, maybe around six years old, something like that. That's where I first saw Roy Palmer.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I lived on Palmer's Avenue and I knew Roy Palmer when he was playing the bass fiddle. I must have been before five years old. And we lived right across the street from one another when I was nothing but a kid.

ctx.x: Yeah, read at my home. And you can imagine, I didn't give Roy a chance to turn it on unless I was asking him something. So Dutre, he was kind of sickly. And he would let me play for him. He'd go back to Curtain and some kind of medicine in hell, a blend in hell, something like asthma. I learned that he was, while in the Navy he was shutting the hole where the gunpowder was and that caused that. So he'd always say to me, he called me Pardner. He'd say Pardner if I had the good lungs that you have in the wind I…
They did cheat the musicians. Yes, yes, yes.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Roy read music. And so I don't see where they got the idea that Uptown the fellas didn't.

ctx.x: Yeah, sure, I know. And Roy did. And Roy did.

Roy read music. And so I don't see where they got the idea that Uptown the fellas didn't. Maybe Dominic was a little, we're good friends, but maybe a little precious because Dominic was from downtown, you see.
Well, I don't think Dominic, some other people told us that, like some people said that Bolden didn't read. Well maybe Bolden didn't.
